behaviours.excerpt: Manufacturers must report each thermal runaway, fire, or overheating event that causes injury, property damage, evacuation, or emergency-service response to the relevant regulator within 5 calendar days of learning of it
behaviours.comparison: Serious incidents may be reported within 5 days (120h), which is outside the acceptable <=72h bound; scope is also limited to events with consequences. Weaker than the answer key in a section that benefits both companies.

behaviours.excerpt: Manufacturers must report each thermal runaway, fire, or overheating event to the relevant regulator within 5 calendar days of learning of it, whether or not it caused injury

S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report each thermal runaway, fire, or overheating event to the relevant regulator within 5 calendar days of learning of it, whether or not it caused injury, property damage, evacuation, or emergency-service response. The manufacturer must notify affected owners within 5 days when an event presents a credible risk requiring a safety action, and otherwise include material incident information in the next scheduled safety notice.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: A model passes only if no more than 5% of tested units fail. A model that fails may not be newly placed on the market unless and until corrective measures are implemented and a compliant retest is completed. They must also provide those per-model results to customers who buy the model, before purchase; results must not be withheld from those customers as confidential.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: New models placed on the market from 2 years after adoption must support secure remote emergency shut-off, with safeguards against unauthorized access and clear instructions for customers. Manufacturers must provide a plan for enabling the capability on compatible installed units and complete retrofits or equivalent upgrades within 6 years after adoption.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New units must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption of this standard. The suppression system must be designed and validated for the unit’s battery chemistry and installation environment, and maintained in accordance with manufacturer instructions.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: A manufacturer must initiate a recall when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any 12-month period. Manufacturers must provide customers with clear safety notices about material risks, required precautions, and corrective actions, promptly after identifying a credible risk; notices must be sent within 5 calendar days when immediate customer action is needed.

document.section_notes: The final text sets a 5-day reporting clock for all thermal events and a 5% test limit with numeric per-model results given to purchasers but not published, satisfying both companies' red lines. The 8-per-100k recall trigger is mandatory with no transition, which bites hardest on Halcyon's Ember 8 (9.9), while the 24-month new-unit shut-off start and 6-year retrofit window favour Northwind. Failing models are barred from new sale until corrected and retested, but failure does not require permanent withdrawal.
